name: Sangai Cafe at Sendra Park
signature_dish: Manipuri thali with nga atoiba thongba
why_it_matters: The lake-view multi-cuisine restaurant inside Sendra Park & Resort, perched on the island after the causeway from Moirang. The only sit-down meal stop with a clean kitchen at the Sendra viewpoint cluster — most lake visitors otherwise eat at floating-homestay shacks or skip lunch.
insider_tip: Order the local Manipuri thali rather than the Chinese menu; the kitchen handles fish-based Meitei dishes much better. Dining hall opens to the lake-view balcony — book the corner table after the morning Sendra Hill climb.
signature_address: Sendra Park & Resort, Sendra Island, Moirang, Bishnupur District, Manipur 795133

name: Loktak Aquamarine Floating Homestay kitchen
why_it_matters: Started by Ashok Sapamcha in 2017 on a single phumdi, this is the working kitchen the floating-homestay scene is built around — meals come from fish caught the same morning by the host family on the lake. The closest a non-resident traveller gets to eating like a Loktak fisherman.
insider_tip: Three meals are included with the homestay rate (~₹1,000/night/head). Day-trippers can pre-arrange a meal-only visit by phone — the boat ride from Phubala ghat is a separate ₹400 round trip. No power on the phumdi, but solar lamps after dark.
signature_address: Champu Khangpok floating village, Loktak Lake, near Phubala ghat, Bishnupur District, Manipur 795133

name: Sendra Tourist Home canteen
why_it_matters: The Manipur Tourism Department's hilltop tourist home runs a no-frills canteen serving the only sit-down meal between Moirang and the Phubala ghat road end. Same dining room serves overnight tourist-lodge guests and walk-ins from the Sendra viewpoint.
insider_tip: Open lunch (12-2:30pm) and dinner (7-9pm) only. Cash-only. Order the day's fish — supplies come up from Thanga ghat in the morning and run out by 1:30pm. Sunset from the canteen balcony is the same view as the paid Sendra viewpoint, without the crowd.
signature_address: Sendra Tourist Home, Sendra hill-top, Ithing, Bishnupur District, Manipur 795133

name: Maipakchao Family Floating Homestay kitchen
why_it_matters: Family-run floating kitchen on a phumdi reached by boat from Thanga ghat — listed by Responsible Tourism India as a community-tourism participant. Meals are cooked over a wood fire by the family that lives on the same phumdi.
insider_tip: Phone ahead — there's no walk-in option, the boatman from Thanga has to be told you're coming. Three meals included with the overnight stay; lunch-only visit possible with two days notice. No alcohol on premises.
signature_address: Maipakchao Family Floating Homestay, near Thanga, Loktak Lake, Bishnupur District, Manipur 795133

name: Chennai Kitchen
why_it_matters: The honest South Indian counter in a hill border town — run by Moreh's 17,000-strong Tamil community (descendants of the 1962 Burma exodus). Filter coffee, idli-vada-sambar, masala dosa and Chettinad chicken on the chalkboard. The diaspora kitchen rather than a Tamil-themed import.
insider_tip: Counter-service style; cash preferred. Walk in from the Tamil Sangam community hall on Paichanveng Road. Closes for lunch on Sunday mornings (community service at the temple). Ask for the day's special — Tamil festival days bring kuzhi paniyaram and rava kesari.
signature_address: Paichanveng, near Tamil Sangam Moreh, Tengnoupal District, Manipur 795131

name: Elora Hotel multi-cuisine restaurant
why_it_matters: Tengnoupal district's first 3-star property runs the only sit-down multi-cuisine restaurant in town that takes reservations. Burmese-influenced khao soi and fish curry sit beside the standard Indian menu — a useful tell of how cross-border food crosses the fence.
insider_tip: Open all day. Hotel's coffee shop on the ground floor is the cleanest non-residence cafe in Moreh; in-house guests get priority on dinner tables when the trader-bus convoy is in town. Cash and card both accepted.
signature_address: Elora Hotel, Moreh, Tengnoupal District, Manipur 795131 (110 km from Imphal on AH-1)

name: Namphalong border-market thohk stalls
why_it_matters: The first row of food stalls past the Namphalong checkpost — wooden makeshift tables that serve Burmese-style thohk (the Myanmar equivalent of Indian chaat). The only place a day-pass Indian visitor can eat Myanmar food without a visa.
insider_tip: Day-pass at Moreh Gate 1 with photo ID, then walk five minutes into Namphalong. Carry small Indian rupee notes and Myanmar kyat — both are accepted. Thohk for breakfast, mohinga rice-noodle soup at lunch. Stalls shut by 4 pm because the gate closes at sunset.
signature_address: Namphalong Market, ~5 min walk past Moreh Friendship Gate 1, Sagaing Region, Myanmar (Indian day-pass area)

name: Tamil Sangam community canteen
why_it_matters: The Tamil Sangam Hall runs a community kitchen on Aadi (July-Aug) and Thai (Jan) festival days that anyone can join — the closest thing Northeast India has to a Tamil temple-meals counter. Rest of the year, members run a small lunch counter for the school next door.
insider_tip: Drop in via the Tamil Sangam Moreh Facebook page contact for current opening hours. Lunch is the safe bet (12-1:30pm). Donation-based on festival days. No alcohol; pure-veg only.
signature_address: Tamil Sangam Hall, Paichanveng Road, Moreh, Tengnoupal District, Manipur 795131

name: 25 Degree North Hotel restaurant
why_it_matters: Sit-down restaurant attached to the hotel of the same name on Phungreitang Hill — windows face Shirui peak. Tangkhul Naga kitchen runs alongside an Indian-Continental menu, with smoked pork and fermented-bamboo dishes that other Ukhrul stays don't bother with.
insider_tip: Phone ahead during Shirui Lily Festival (May-June) — the dining room books out for festival speakers. Off-season, walk-in is fine. Order across both menus: Tangkhul plate plus a continental main.
signature_address: 25 Degree North Hotel, Phungreitang Hill, Ukhrul, Manipur 795142

name: Champhai Tourist Lodge restaurant
why_it_matters: The Mizoram Tourism / Art & Culture Department lodge at Champhai operates the most reliable kitchen in town — Mizo bai (vegetable stew) and vawksa rep (smoked pork) cooked the way official-circuit tours expect. Same dining room serves overnight guests and walk-in lunches.
insider_tip: Open lunch 12:30-2:30pm and dinner 7-9pm only. Cash preferred — card readers fail in monsoon. Sunday meals run lighter; book the day before. Phone the lodge (03831-23866) to confirm dinner is on if you arrive late.
signature_address: Tourist Lodge, Champhai, Champhai District, Mizoram 796321

name: Hotel Hranga Plaza restaurant
why_it_matters: Hranga Plaza is a recently constructed hotel in central Champhai — the in-house restaurant fills the gap between the government tourist-lodge canteen and the Holiday Home dining room. Multi-cuisine but Mizo plates remain the strong suit; Indian-Chinese options for vegetarian travellers.
insider_tip: Walk in for lunch (12-2:30pm) or dinner (6:30-9pm). The bazaar location means it fills on market days (Wednesday/Saturday) — go early. Phone 03831-2340217 to check dinner availability.
signature_address: Hotel Hranga Plaza, Champhai bazaar, Champhai District, Mizoram 796321

name: Champhai-Hnahlan Winery tasting room
why_it_matters: Champhai & Hnahlan Grape Winery Ltd, established 2007, is the first winery in Mizoram — Zawlaidi (Love Potion) was first released September 2010 and remains India's only grape wine made in a fully-prohibition state under a separate state Wine Act. Tasting room runs out of the Hnahlan production unit.
insider_tip: Book the visit on +91 96155 58341 — drop-ins not entertained. The Hnahlan unit is 30 km from Champhai bazaar towards the Myanmar border; carry your ILP. Grape harvest: April-May. Adults only; no on-the-spot bottle purchases — order through the winery and collect at Aizawl.
signature_address: Champhai-Hnahlan Grape Winery Ltd, Hnahlan village, Champhai District, Mizoram 796321

name: Hotel Holiday Home dining hall
why_it_matters: Hotel Holiday Home is a town-centre property listed by the Champhai district tourism office; its dining hall is the simpler walk-in option for travellers who prefer in-town location over the lodge's hill-top setting.
insider_tip: Open all-day for hotel guests, 12-2:30pm and 7-9pm for walk-ins. Phone 03831-234871 for table booking. Cash and UPI; cards inconsistent. Greens-and-rice plate is the budget order.
signature_address: Hotel Holiday Home, Champhai town centre, Champhai District, Mizoram 796321

name: Lunglei Tourist Lodge restaurant
why_it_matters: The Mizoram Tourism Department's hilltop lodge at Zotlang is the official Lunglei stop on the Tourism Department circuit and runs a multi-cuisine kitchen with Mizo plates as the strong suit. Clean, predictable, and the only sit-down dinner in town that's reliably open after 8 pm.
insider_tip: Open lunch 12:30-2:30pm and dinner 7-9pm. The dining hall faces the southern ridge — book a window-side table for the Lunglei sunrise. Cash preferred; UPI works but card readers are unreliable.
signature_address: Tourist Lodge, Zotlang, Lunglei-Thenzawl Road, Lunglei, Mizoram 796701

name: Hotel Elite multi-cuisine kitchen
why_it_matters: Town-side hotel on a hillock with a small restaurant — the in-town counterpart to the Tourist Lodge for travellers who skip the Zotlang hilltop. Mizo and standard-Indian menu, deluxe rooms with deluxe-only dining hours.
insider_tip: Walk in for breakfast 7-10 am and dinner 7-9 pm. The kitchen runs lean — order ahead if you want bai with smoked pork (the cook starts it from raw). Sunday lunch service is patchy.
signature_address: Hotel Elite, Lunglei, Lunglei District, Mizoram 796701

name: Momo Hut
why_it_matters: Lunglei's recognised momo joint in the Lunglawn locality — fillings cover veg, chicken, pork and beef. Counter-style with bench seating; the cleanest snack option between Zotlang and the bazaar.
insider_tip: Open evenings (4-9pm) and weekend lunches. Walk-in only. Cash preferred. Pork momos are the order — chicken plate is honest but not the kitchen's strength.
signature_address: Momo Hut, Lunglawn, Lunglei District, Mizoram 796701

name: Tourist Lodge hilltop tea-counter
why_it_matters: The lodge's outdoor tea counter on the highest point in Lunglei is where lodge staff serve sunrise and sunset chai with Mizo sasong biscuits. Free to walk in even if you're not staying — the only sit-down sunrise spot in town.
insider_tip: Open 5:30-7:30 am and 4:30-6 pm for the views. No menu — point and order. Mid-October to early March is the best clear-sky window. Carry your own water; the counter only runs hot drinks.
signature_address: Tourist Lodge tea counter, Zotlang, Lunglei-Thenzawl Road, Lunglei, Mizoram 796701
